  Color palettes are predefined sets of colors that serve as the foundation of our design system. Each palette groups together brand, neutral, and functional colors (such as primary, gray, success, warning, and other colors) into a consistent and reusable collection.

  By using color palettes, you ensure that components across the product share a consistent visual language. Instead of hardcoding values, you reference the palette variables, which makes it easy to:

  - Maintain consistency across all UI elements

  - Apply themes or brand updates quickly

  - Keep accessibility in mind with contrast-ready color pairs

  In practice, palettes act as the single source of truth for color usage. Updating a value in the palette automatically propagates through the entire framework, keeping design and code perfectly aligned.

  For example, let’s say your design system provides the following color palette:

  <div className={styles.colorList}>
    <div className={styles.colorItem}>
      <span className={`${styles.colorSwatch} ${styles.colorPrimary}`}></span>
      <div>
        <p className={styles.colorLabel}>Primary <span className={styles.colorCode}>#F34E4E</span></p>
      </div>
    </div>
    <div className={styles.colorItem}>
      <span className={`${styles.colorSwatch} ${styles.colorSecondary}`}></span>
      <div>
        <p className={styles.colorLabel}>Secondary <span className={styles.colorCode}>#FFF6EA</span></p>
      </div>
    </div>
    <div className={styles.colorItem}>
      <span className={`${styles.colorSwatch} ${styles.colorAction}`}></span>
      <div>
        <p className={styles.colorLabel}>Action <span className={styles.colorCode}>#7BB9FA</span></p>
      </div>
    </div>
    <div className={styles.colorItem}>
      <span className={`${styles.colorSwatch} ${styles.colorGrey}`}></span>
      <div>
        <p className={styles.colorLabel}>Surface <span className={styles.colorCode}>#EBEBEB</span></p>
      </div>
    </div>
    <div className={styles.colorItem}>
      <span className={`${styles.colorSwatch} ${styles.colorBlack}`}></span>
      <div>
        <p className={styles.colorLabel}>Black <span className={styles.colorCode}>#282828</span></p>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>

  You can transform it into a usable SCSS palette as follows:

  - First, add the igniteui-theming package to your .scss file:

  ```scss
  @use 'igniteui-theming/' as *; 
  ```

  - Then add the supplied design system colors to a variable to create a palette.
  You can have two kinds of palettes: a [manually created palette](manually-created-palettes), where you directly add all color values you want your palette to have, or an [auto-generated palette](auto-generated-palettes), where you use the color generation functions to create a full palette based on just a few key colors.
  
  - For this example, we will create an auto-generated palette. Supply the provided design system color values as a map to the [palette()](auto-generated-palettes) function.

  ```scss 
  $my-palette: palette(
    $primary: #f34e4e,
    $secondary: #fff6ea,
    $surface: #ebebeb
  );
  ```

  - By using the [palette()](auto-generated-palettes) function, apart from the supplied color, it also generates additional 11 variants per group, plus a contrast color for each of the variants. 

  - After we created our palette, we are ready to include it in our project with the [palette mixin](palette-mixin). This will generate CSS variables based on the map that we created with the [palette()](auto-generated-palettes) function. 

  ```scss
  @include palette($my-palette);
  ```

  - This will generate CSS variables for each color in the palette, which you can then use throughout your stylesheets. The supplied color value becomes the `500{:js}` variant of that color group and the other lighter and darker variants goes from `50{:js}` to `900{:js}`. 
  
  - To reference a color from the generated palette, you can use the [color()](accessing-the-css-variables) function, for the color variants and the [contrast-color()](accessing-the-css-variables) function for the contrast colors. For example:

  ```scss
  .demo-box {
    background: color($color: 'primary', $variant: 600);
    color: contrast-color($color: 'primary', $variant: 600);
  }
  ```

  By using the generated CSS variables, you can easily apply your design system colors across your application while keeping your styles organized and maintainable.
